```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Every number of the expected-numbers section is read from the committed data
# files of the case, so that the guide and the pages cannot drift apart; readr
# rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA.
fmt <- \(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) |> sub(pattern = "^-", replacement = "−")

curve <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
analysts <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
marks <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/reference_marks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
power <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_power.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ri <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_ri.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
n_emails <- nrow(readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/housing_audit.csv", show_col_types = FALSE))

ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
ref_all <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                        uncoded = "drop", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))
an <- \(id, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id]
mark <- \(id) marks$b_pp[marks$id == id]
shift <- \(axis, option, col = "shift_mean") deviations[[col]][deviations$axis == axis & deviations$option == option]
pw <- \(design, gap) power$power[startsWith(power$design, design) & power$gap_pp == gap]
reply_gap <- datawizard::data_filter(outcomes, outcome == "reply" & contrast == "hispanic")
# The SCORE replication on the scale of the course (display_replication.csv)
replication <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
rep_val <- \(population_code, authorities_code, col) {
  replication[[col]][replication$population == population_code &
                       replication$authorities == authorities_code]
}
sgn <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(if (round(x, d) >= 0) "+" else "", fmt(x, d))

# The Task 3 table: Hispanic against all other names among the coded replies
coded <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(ProperName)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup))
tab_8ptrz <- stats::xtabs(~ hispanic_name + ProperName, data = coded)  # r-style: keep – the table that chisq.test() takes
chi_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz)$statistic)
chi_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# Placement as try_spec() prints it: the specifications further below zero,
# with the tolerance of the helpers, so that the logit twin of the reference
# specification ties with it
placement_ref <- sum(curve$b_pp < ref$b_pp - 1e-9)
other_max <- deviations |>
  datawizard::data_filter(axis != "population") |>
  datawizard::data_summary(m = max(shift_max)) |>
  datawizard::data_extract("m")
```

::: {.callout-note}
**This document is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. It holds the run sheet of the one-day course (deck `slides/housing-one-day.qmd`) and of the short session (deck `slides/housing-short.qmd`), the checks before a delivery, the expected numbers and the fallbacks. The participant pages under `tracks/` carry the same timings without the instructor guidance.
:::

## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the opening page advertises no delivery. Scheduling one takes three steps, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue, event, mode, registration URL), set `track: housing-one-day` or `track: housing-short`, and set `active: 'true'`. Render the opening page (`quarto render index.qmd`), and it shows a "Next delivery" callout with a link to the track. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide on recording. If you record, record the talk only, announce it at the start of each recorded stretch, and pause it for the hands-on tasks. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Decide which way the day leans. The one-day deck keeps two kinds of optional run on the `d` key: `tools` (five slides in the tools segment of Part 1 and the nine-slide R tutorial of Part 2) and `methods` (the six-slide methods tutorial of Part 3 and the two slides of multiverse background in Part 4). To make a run part of the main flow, list it under `core-runs:` in the YAML of `slides/housing-one-day.qmd` and render the deck again; a run that is not listed stays optional and can still be switched on live.

**Resetting, before the next delivery.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and keep it as a dated snapshot, for example `cases/housing/data/class_results_2026-11-06.csv`.
- [ ] Clear the data rows of the Sheet, so that the chart opens almost empty for the next class. Do not touch the Form, the Worker or the field schema; only the rows change from one class to the next.

---

## Before the day

### The week before

- [ ] **The workspace repository.** The pages of the case are part of the course site (`CodeMoreh/applied-replication`), but the workspace (`CodeMoreh/replication-lab-housing`) does not exist on GitHub yet, and every address that points at it is a placeholder until it does: the workspace zip on the setup page and the cheatsheet, the workspace address on the tools slide of Part 1, and the links in the README of the workspace. Create the repository, push it, and download the zip once from its public address to confirm that it unzips into `replication-lab-housing-main`.
- [ ] **The class-results Form.** Out of the box, the housing helpers submit to the results Form that every case shares, the one set up for the EU-frames case, and the housing chart reads the same Sheet through the same Worker, keeping only the rows whose label carries the word `housing` after the tag. That works as it stands. Clear the Sheet of the rows of earlier deliveries before the day (the data rows below the header of the tab "Form Responses 1"; the Form keeps working), because the EU-frames chart reads every row and would draw housing rows as unclassed diamonds. The alternative, which keeps the two classes apart for good, is a Form of its own, about twenty minutes once, following `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`: copy the Form, link a new Sheet, deploy a second Worker, and wire the new codes into the four marked blocks that the note lists.
- [ ] **Joining instructions.** Send the address of the track page, the setup page (with the request to run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK before the day, and to bring a laptop and its charger), the case study as the pre-reading, and the help page.
- [ ] **The tab switching.** Click once through the sequence of Parts 3 and 4 (deck → specification menu and decision map → the Multiverse page and back), which is the one sequence that you run live several times in the day.
- [ ] **The room.** Confirm the projector, the power sockets, the wifi for visitors (webR downloads its engine and packages on first load) and whether the room has Vevox or a similar response tool. The slides say "type in chat" for the four held answers of the day; in the room, decide in advance what "chat" means; the cue sheet below sets out the options.

### The night before

- [ ] Render the site. Pause pCloud first, because a full `quarto render` of a project inside a pCloud folder dies on renamed files; otherwise render page by page. Check that the opening page, both track sections, the case pages and both decks are current, and push if the site is published.
- [ ] **The live-results loop.** Submit one test result from the browser lab (`try_spec()`, then `submit_exploration(nickname = "test-row")`), confirm that it reaches the Sheet, press *Run Code* on the class chart of the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) page and find the test circle. Then delete the test row from the Sheet.
- [ ] **The workspace, as a participant meets it.** Download the zip afresh, unzip it, open the folder in your IDE, run `source("R/check_setup.R")` (every line OK, the last at −19.97 points), complete the preregistration block with a dummy specification and render the report.
- [ ] **The browser lab, cold.** Open the live page of the lab in a private window on a connection like that of the venue, time the load of the R engine, and run the setup cell and the Task 3 cell (14.265).
- [ ] **The public record.** Confirm that the three addresses of the records slide load without an account: doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU, osf.io/3a8bg and osf.io/2ug8x, and that the final report of the replication is findable from the last one, because it is the target of the three-minute search in Part 4. The de-identified data of the replication are in its sub-component osf.io/xseqg, for anyone who asks.
- [ ] **The fallback zip.** Put the workspace zip on a USB stick, for anyone whose download fails in the room.
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card (below) as a ready-to-paste text, and charge everything.

### Opening the room

- [ ] Put the address of the course site, the browser lab and the cheatsheet on the screen or the whiteboard as people arrive, with the wifi details.
- [ ] Hand out the green and red sticky notes, or open the response tool, and say what each means: green, working; red, stuck.
- [ ] Keep four tabs ready: the deck, the [decision map](../cases/housing/map.qmd), the [specification menu](../cases/housing/menu.qmd) and the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) page.
- [ ] If you record, announce it now and say what is and is not recorded.

## Run sheet – the one-day course

Times in the part tables are relative: 0:00 is the start of that part. The clock below maps them onto the day.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust.** Newcastle on Friday 6 November 2026 is on GMT, because British Summer Time ends on 25 October. The default below starts at 10:00 and keeps the breaks of the slides (thirty minutes, an hour, thirty minutes), so the day ends at 18:00. A 09:30 start ends at 17:30. Shorter breaks need the text of the break slides changed as well (`slides/_segments/shared/_break1.qmd`, `_lunch.qmd`, `_break2.qmd`).
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Newcastle (GMT) |
|---|---|---|
| Part 1 – Credibility and tools | 0:00–1:30 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Break | 1:30–2:00 | 11:30–12:00 |
| Part 2 – The claim and its estimand | 2:00–3:30 | 12:00–13:30 |
| Lunch | 3:30–4:30 | 13:30–14:30 |
| Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration | 4:30–6:00 | 14:30–16:00 |
| Break | 6:00–6:30 | 16:00–16:30 |
| Part 4 – Multiverse, replication and preregistration | 6:30–8:00 | 16:30–18:00 |

**Four stretches of the deck are optional**, marked on screen and switched in one keystroke: the five tools slides of Part 1, the R tutorial of Part 2 (nine slides), the methods tutorial of Part 3 (six slides) and the multiverse background of Part 4 (two slides). The timings below assume that you walk about half of each. Walking all of them in full costs about fifteen minutes that the day does not have, and skipping them all leaves the hands-on tasks more room than they need.

### Deck controls {#deck-controls}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space · right arrow · clicker | next slide, always exactly one: the deck is linear, so that no clicker press can skip a part |
| **`d`** | switch between the **extended** and the **lean** deck, live; in lean mode the optional slides are taken out of the deck and every key skips them |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the next or the previous part |
| **`g`** | jump bar: type a few letters of any slide title and press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view, with the notes, a timer and the next slide |
| **`f`** · **`esc`** | full screen · slide overview |

The readout at the top right names the part and the position, and its badge shows the state of the deck: green **extended**, burgundy **optional** on a slide of an optional run, amber **lean** when the runs are off, with a burgundy dot where a run has been lifted out. Adding `?depth=0` to the address opens the deck lean. The first slide of each optional run carries a small grey link that jumps to where the main flow resumes.

## Run sheet – the short session

The short session runs on `slides/housing-short.qmd` as two halves of about seventy-five minutes with a break of fifteen. It has no Task 2 at the keyboard (the estimand statement is written as a held answer, and the graph is followed on the slides) and no Task 5, which `tracks/housing-short/after.qmd` sets as work for afterwards. Its one optional run is the two slides of multiverse background.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust**, here for an afternoon slot from 14:00. For a slot of two hours, drop the multiverse background, take the SCORE slides of the first half at speed, and shorten the replication to three slides (the design, the result, and robustness against replicability); the reproduction and the exploration keep their full time.
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Example clock (GMT) |
|---|---|---|
| First half – The claim and its reproduction | 0:00–1:15 | 14:00–15:15 |
| Break | 1:15–1:30 | 15:15–15:30 |
| Second half – Exploration and replication | 1:30–2:45 | 15:30–16:45 |

## The held answers {#held-answers}

Four times in the day, and three times in the short session, the class writes an answer, holds it and releases it together: the estimand statement (Part 2), the reproduced $\chi^2$ (Part 3), the placement (Part 4) and "declared" before the preregistered run (Part 4, one-day only). Holding the answers keeps each one independent of the others, and releasing them together is what produces the wall of identical values after the reproduction. The slides say "type in chat"; the cue sheet below says what that means in the room.

**The reproduction moment.** Everyone runs the Task 3 code, in the workspace or in the lab. When most of the class has a number: "Type your X-squared, hold it … go." The target is **$\chi^2$ = `r fmt(chi_yates, 3)`**, the value recorded for 8PTRZ. A participant with `r fmt(chi_plain, 2)` has passed `correct = FALSE`, which is the opening line of the next slide. A participant with another number has kept the uncoded replies or filtered on a different column; check that the filter is `!is.na(ProperName)`.

**The catch-up card**, for the re-entry to Part 3:

> Just back? You have missed nothing that you cannot recover: (1) if Task 2 is unfinished, run the graph chunk as it stands and come back to the wording later; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – the target is chi-square = 14.265, and the full code is on the slide and in the browser lab; (3) Task 4 is exploration, so try two specifications and submit one. Put up a red note and I will come to you during Task 4.

## In person and online {#cue-sheet}

The materials are the same in both settings. What changes is how people answer, flag trouble and pair up.

| Beat | In person (Newcastle) | Online |
|---|---|---|
| Held answers | the response tool of the room if it has one; otherwise written on a card and held up on "go" | typed in chat, sent on "go" |
| Working or stuck | green and red sticky notes on the laptop lid | a green circle or "STUCK" in chat |
| Rescues | the facilitator circulates | the problem shown on the shared screen |
| The live chart | on the projector, and on the laptops | everyone opens the Multiverse page |
| Form links | on the screen | pasted in chat |
| Breaks | the countdown slide and the time aloud | the countdown slide and "back at :xx" in chat |

---

## The cutting order {#cutting-order}

When time runs short, cut from the optional runs before anything else, so that the time comes out of a tutorial before it comes out of a task.

- **Part 1** – at 0:30, cut the data-availability slide of Miske et al. to one line and the open-research table to one sentence a row. At 0:58, leave the optional tools run switched off.
- **Part 2** – at 0:34, drop selection and feedback to one sentence. At 1:02, skip the R tutorial. At 1:22, Task 2 becomes a demonstration, finished over lunch.
- **Part 3** – at 0:50, the methods run stays off. At 1:05, Task 4 shortens to two calls of `try_spec()` and a submission, but everybody still submits.
- **Part 4** – at 0:10, skip the multiverse background. At 0:50, show the three-minute search on the shared screen instead of setting it.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table · the held estimand statement · the box around the reply · the reproduction and its held answer · the Task 4 submission · robustness against replicability · the preregistration moment.

## Fallbacks {#fallbacks}

Each row names the first move, not the only one, and every ladder ends at a point from which the session can carry on.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **An installation fails on the day** | The browser lab holds the whole exercise and gives the same numbers; the participant carries on there, and the workspace survives for later. |
| **The workspace download fails in the room** | The zip on the USB stick. |
| **The browser lab stalls** | The ladder of the [cheatsheet](../cases/housing/cheatsheet.qmd): a hard reload and the cells above run again, then a second browser, then the shared screen, then the by-hand lookup, in which the facilitator reads the five choices off `spec_curve.csv` and submits the row through the Form. Everyone still gets a mark. |
| **The wifi fails** | The workspace runs offline once its packages are installed, so Tasks 1–5 continue; only the submissions wait. Collect the printed results (the tag, the label, `b`, `se`, `t`, `df`, `n`, `r`) and submit them through the Form when the network returns. The browser lab needs the network for its first load. |
| **The live chart fails** (Form, Worker, CORS) | The chart falls back to the committed `cases/housing/data/class_results.csv`, which holds only its header. Pull the Sheet as CSV, put it in place of that file, render the Multiverse page locally and share the screen. The static curve and the reference marks at the top of the page are enough for the debrief. Submissions are safe in the Sheet whatever happens to the chart. |
| **The OSF is slow during the three-minute search** | Show the report of the replication on the shared screen; the beat still works. Nothing in the tasks depends on the OSF. |
| **A participant has lost their tag** | It is in `.class-tag` at the root of the workspace; in the lab, `report_result(nickname = "their-tag")` reuses it. |

## Expected numbers {#expected-numbers}

- **Task 1.** The last check of `R/check_setup.R`: the reference specification reproduces at `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` percentage points.
- **Task 2.** `r format(n_emails, big.mark = ",")` emails, 23 bounced, 991 delivered, 563 replies, 5 without a greeting code, 558 coded. Greeted by name among the coded replies: white 61.1%, Black 56.1%, Hispanic 41.2%; Santiago lowest at 37.1%. The graph: with every delivered email counted, `adjustmentSets()` returns the empty set, because the name was assigned at random; `paths(dag, Z = "reply")` reports the paths through the official and through the community as open. Adding the community to `Z` closes the second, and nothing can close the first, because nobody observed the official.
- **Task 3.** $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(chi_yates, 3)` on `r an("8PTRZ", "n_recorded")` coded replies with the continuity correction, the value recorded for 8PTRZ; `r fmt(chi_plain, 3)` without it. The optional logit of UYV3F: z = `r fmt(an("UYV3F", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` on `r an("UYV3F", "n_recorded")` replies to Hispanic and white names.
- **The reference specification** (white names, replies, uncoded dropped, linear model, no covariates): `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref$rate_comp)`%), t = `r fmt(ref$stat, 2)` on `r ref$df` df, n = `r ref$n`. Its twin on every delivered email: `r fmt(ref_all$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref_all$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref_all$rate_comp)`%), n = `r ref_all$n`.
- **The curve.** `r nrow(curve)` specifications, all below zero and all significant at 5% under the test of the model, from `r fmt(min(curve$b_pp))` to `r fmt(max(curve$b_pp))` points; the largest p is `r fmt(max(curve$p), 4)`, and the largest randomisation p is `r fmt(max(curve$p_ri), 4)`. Counting every delivered email moves the estimate by `r fmt(shift("population", "all"), 2)` points on average (from `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_min"), 2)` to `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_max"), 2)`); every other decision by at most `r fmt(other_max, 2)`. No pair changes its sign or its significance.
- **Placement.** The reference specification is placed at `r placement_ref`: no specification of the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it. A placement of 32 or more comes from counting every delivered email, because all 32 specifications that count the replies lie further below zero.
- **The reference marks.** OAs 2017 `r fmt(mark("OA"))` points (z = −3.73, N = 549); 8PTRZ `r fmt(mark("8PTRZ"))`; UYV3F `r fmt(mark("UYV3F"))`; EWFMI `r fmt(mark("EWFMI"))`; 25N5D `r fmt(mark("25N5D"))`; P9W8Y `r fmt(mark("P9W8Y"))`, placed by the course refit because Multi100 recorded no statistic for it. The published model refitted on the blinded thirds: `r fmt(mark("OA_blinded"))` points, not on the chart.
- **Replies.** The gap in any reply between Hispanic and white names is `r fmt(reply_gap$b_pp)` points, two-sided p = `r fmt(reply_gap$p, 2)`; the paper reports p = .11 with a one-tailed test.
- **Randomisation.** Reshuffling the names among the coded replies gives gaps between `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.025))` and `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.975))` points in 95% of `r format(nrow(ri), big.mark = ",")` reshuffles.
- **Power.** The original comparison, about 181 replies a group at a white share of 61%: `r fmt(pw("original", 20), 2)` for a gap of 20 points, `r fmt(pw("original", 13), 2)` for 13, `r fmt(pw("original", 10), 2)` for 10. The replication, 369 a group: `r fmt(pw("replication", 10), 2)` for 10 points.
- **The replication** (from its final report, osf.io/2ug8x): 3,050 authorities emailed, 1,811 replies; on the 1,243 replies of the authorities matched to census data, logit with the demographic covariates of the paper from the 2018 ACS (no Hard Email), b = 0.098 (SE 0.149), z = 0.66, p = 0.511 on a random draw of 738, and z = 0.44, p = 0.657 on all 1,243. The preregistered linear model was not significant "approximately 93 percent of the time". At most +2.45 points in favour of the Hispanic names. The de-identified data are public at osf.io/xseqg (folder "Public Data": `Audit_Deidentified.dta`, the analysis do-file and a dictionary, licence unstated, so the course links to them and does not copy them). On the scale of the course (`cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv`), the gap is `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("replies", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies (`r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_hisp"))`% against `r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_comp"))`%), `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "b_pp"))` among the `r format(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies of sub-county authorities, and `r sgn(rep_val("all", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("all", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` emails in the de-identified file, none of them significant (smallest p = `r fmt(min(replication$p), 2)`). The logit with covariates in thirds on the 1,243 sub-county replies that carry every covariate (one of the 1,244 lacks the poverty third) gives b = 0.051, z = 0.45, column 4 of the report.
- **The five analysts.** Three concluded "evidence for the claim" in Task 1 of Multi100 (8PTRZ, UYV3F, EWFMI) and two "no evidence either way" (25N5D, judging the claim by the twenty points of the abstract; P9W8Y, whose Task 1 model tested the female names only).

## Debrief questions {#debrief}

Choose by what the class chart shows, not by the order below.

1. **The step in the curve.** "Who counted every delivered email? What question does your estimate answer that the estimate of the paper does not, and which one is the claim?"
2. **The decision that did nothing.** "Who changed the model from the linear probability model to the logit and found that the estimate barely moved? Why does it barely move here, when the coefficients look so different?"
3. **Justification.** "Whose causal graph settled their choice of emails? Whose graph could have justified both choices equally well?"
4. **The two verdicts of no evidence.** "Two analysts ticked 'no evidence', although the work of each shows a significant gap. What were they judging the claim by?"
5. **Placement.** "Your placement puts you among 64 justifiable alternatives. What does an analyst at the end of the curve owe the reader that an analyst in the middle does not?"
6. **Robustness against replication.** "Every specification on these data finds the gap; the replication did not. Which result should a housing authority act on, and what would you want to know first?"
7. **The names.** "Santiago and Gabriela against Joe Garcia and Michael Hernandez. What does a name manipulate besides ethnicity?"
8. **How preregistration felt.** "Did writing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed? Would you have chosen differently after the exploration?"
